vision.one_liner: Just talk to VP. It builds the calling agent, cleans your list, gets your number and makes calls your customers are glad to take.
vision.promise: Just talk to VP. It builds the agent, cleans your list, gets your number and makes calls your customers are glad to take, in their language and inside the rules. Then it shows you every call, every rupee, and what it will do better next time.
vision.for_whom: Indian businesses (SMB to enterprise) with a recurring reason to call their own customers: insurance intermediaries, lenders, subscriptions and utilities, clinics, education, consented real-estate inquiries. First jobs are post-sale service calls (renewal, pre-due EMI, appointment reminders). Not cold outbound, not consumer-internet firms with in-house teams.
vision.status: Blueprint for owner review, 2026-10-21. Nothing has run on a live Indian call or with a buyer yet; VP scores in this page are design targets.

pillars.name: Talk is the front door
pillars.line: Typed or spoken Hinglish; VP's agents do the work through the same tools any developer gets.

pillars.name: The call is the product
pillars.line: Warm, quick, honest Hinglish voice that opens with something useful and never wastes time.

pillars.name: Honest by construction
pillars.line: Disclosure, crisis lines, no OTP or payment asks are code predicates at one reply door, not prompt text.

pillars.name: India and compliance by default
pillars.line: Call category first; one dial path; A2P pack; every call shows why it was allowed.

pillars.name: Results are earned
pillars.line: Outcomes from systems of record; cost per earned outcome is the client's north star.

pillars.name: Remember with permission
pillars.line: Quoted, playable, forgettable memory; preferences auto with undo; nothing pooled across tenants.

pillars.name: Learn honestly
pillars.line: Fast lane for catastrophic lines; fixed-horizon tests, A/A checks and expiry for the rest.

pillars.name: One honest price
pillars.line: All-in INR per connected second, caps on workspace, campaign and key, estimate before launch.

journey.stage: 1. Hear it, then sign up (0-1 min)

journey.vp_agents_do: Public Operator discloses once, asks about the business, plays how a customer would hear it in three registers
journey.client_sees: One orb with live captions, voice cards with India first-audio and INR/min, 'her replies took 1.4 s median on this call (n=9)'
journey.wow: A voice before a form, honest about being an AI and about its speed
journey.competitor_contrast: Sarvam's demo claimed to be human 6/6 times; Retell asks for a Persona ID before any country

journey.client_says_or_does: 'Motor renewal reminders, 1,200 customers' plus a website or brochure
journey.vp_agents_do: Strategist sets job, category and outcome; Brief writer turns the site into facts with quoted spans; at most one question per turn
journey.client_sees: Plan card ('VP does 1-6 now; 7 waits for you'), facts card to approve or strike, readiness rail
journey.wow: Whole job planned and drafts already running
journey.competitor_contrast: Sarvam's prompt box makes only an agent; Retell's checklist covers its canvas

journey.stage: 3. Pick her voice by ear (about 1 min)
journey.client_says_or_does: Hears three voices say one Hinglish line with the brand name; says 'thoda slow bolo, discount mat bolna'
journey.vp_agents_do: Brief writer compiles, lints recitable lines; Test pilot pre-runs six simulated callers
journey.client_sees: Brief as cards with locked disclosure row, predicted reply gap and all-in INR in header, diff card per tweak
journey.wow: Speed and price beside every voice; mismatched voices refused
journey.competitor_contrast: Retell has 0 Indian voices; ElevenLabs accepted an American voice on a Hindi agent

journey.stage: 4. First test call (browser under 3 min; own phone within 15 min)
journey.client_says_or_does: 'Call me in the browser', then 'Kaisi lagi?'; then 'Ring my phone' via missed call
journey.vp_agents_do: Test pilot runs a made-up customer; feedback becomes diffs with one-tap re-test; Line keeper verifies the phone spoof-safely
journey.client_sees: Live captions, reply gap and cut-in marks per turn, 'already said' ledger, door events
journey.wow: Feedback by talking becomes a reviewed change; own phone rings within minutes
journey.competitor_contrast: Bolna tests only by phone; Exotel's web call is 'coming soon'

journey.stage: 5. Data in: any file to an audience (5 min or less)
journey.client_says_or_does: Drops a CSV, Excel, Sheet or text PDF, or connects a CRM: 'isko fire karo'

journey.wow: No file rejected for one bad row; people who already paid are not called
journey.competitor_contrast: Vapi turns a 10-digit mobile into +98 and rejects the file; Retell imports +91 as +1; Exotel drops duplicates silently

journey.client_says_or_does: 'Kal se chalao'; rents a number in their name or connects a carrier; uploads KYC once

journey.client_sees: One launch card: who, when, 20 s sample from a real row, checks, money, outcome; hold 1.2 s to launch
journey.wow: Launch explains itself; tests continue while KYC waits
journey.competitor_contrast: 0 of 6 campaign forms carry consent, DND or DLT; Vapi and Retell disable Launch with no reason

architecture.layer: Control plane (TypeScript, Postgres in India, Azure Container Apps)
architecture.note: Issues a signed call ticket per attempt (version, manifest, variables, memory brief, reservation).

architecture.layer: Engines in code (no agent can override)

Numbers stay in the tenant's name; VP drives the line and never carries calls itself.
Retention chosen at onboarding, never indefinite.

steps: Watch every call: hang-up hazard per script moment with intervals
Fast lane flags a catastrophic line (about call 13-15 for a 90% line)
Throttle that script to 25% and send a fix card to the approver's phone
Coach drafts a fix as shapes; 18 simulated callers x 3 seeds
Gates throw: lint, budget, locked-section diff, provenance, manipulation lint, latency
Human approves with a hash-bound hold (or v2 standing envelope)
Fixed-horizon test with verdict hidden; shadow A/A per tenant
Promote, expire in 60 days, log in 'How she changed for you'
what_learns: Best time inside the legal window
Register and voice only via blind listener panels (v3)
guardrails: Never learned (locked in code): disclosure, recording notice, consent and opt-out, crisis lines, identity, prices and dates, promotion fence, reply-door predicates
Only risk-lowering actions are automatic: revert, throttle, stop
Auto-stop on opt-outs, complaints, disclosure, crisis, reg 21A, minutes per agenda-done call
At most 3 new cards a day; one proposal cycle a day inside the INR 200 test budget
Simulators run on test quota only; a model never grades its own work
No cross-tenant pooling; 'learns on its own' blocked below L4 unless the envelope copy is adopted
learning_loop.cadence: Fast lane: from call 1, fix card to phone within 15 min p90. Slow lane: one proposal cycle a day, tests run 7-28 days, winners expire at 60 days. Bandits only at 1,000+ connected calls a day on one script (v3).

consent: Tenant is the DPDP fiduciary; VP is the processor, with purpose and basis per fact
Consent records are append-only; imports never clear suppression
Seven write gates before any fact is stored; a never-stored list (mood scores, inferred caste, age or health, ID numbers)
Authority by subject: the person wins on preferences and opt-out; systems win on money and dates
Forget follows the person across facts, recordings, channels and CRM, with a tombstone and receipt
Minors excluded; India region; no pooling across tenants
On shared or unverified numbers, memory loads only after an in-call knowledge check

targets: Billed per connected second; unanswered, busy, failed, blocked and VP-fault calls are not billed
Gross margin p50 at least 30% in 2026 and 25% after known 2027 changes, never by downgrading the voice
Effective price at 30/45/90 s: VP 3.49-3.99 vs Sarvam PAYG 7.40/5.20/5.07, Bolna 5.72/7.63/5.72 (rate-card arithmetic, no invoice read)
Pre-registered ladder: 2.99 at COGS 1.94 or less; 2.49 at 1.62; 1.99 at 1.29, after two months of measured cost reconciled within 5%
Caps per workspace, campaign and API key; reservation before each dial; live calls never cut for money
Free trial INR 500 lifetime per verified phone; invoice and NEFT above INR 15,000 a month
Honest limit: not INR 2 at launch; Sarvam Business is cheaper on whole-minute calls

budget.best_measured: 95 ms neural warm; 624 ms Gemini Flash-Lite TTS

speed.note: Cut-ins must be 5% or less on a stereo handset battery. Today only the Indic stack is predicted inside 1.5 s (1.2-1.6 s); no stack passes the cut-in bar (15-42%). The default waits for the joint speed and turn-taking gate; a slower favourite (Natural, predicted 2.0-2.5 s) is offered with its wait shown.

open_decisions.question: 1. Default stack and the speed-voice rule
options: Best whole-call ear rating among stacks that pass the joint speed gate
open_decisions.recommendation: Ear judges whole calls at the handset; Natural stays opt-in with its wait shown until it passes.

open_decisions.question: 2. Base price and unit
options: Per connected second, Base by margin rule (INR 3.49-3.99 today)
Launch at INR 2 and absorb the loss
open_decisions.recommendation: Per second, all-in display; if the ear's pick needs more than 3.99, keep the voice and choose a 4.49 step or lower 2027 margin; reach INR 2 by the ladder.

open_decisions.question: 3. First design partners
options: At least one non-BFSI partner in v0.5
open_decisions.recommendation: Non-BFSI first; insurance and lending after KC5 and KC8.

open_decisions.question: 4. Numbers inside VP
options: Ask carriers for rental in the tenant's name
open_decisions.recommendation: Ask in the quote round; bring-your-own as the second path.

open_decisions.question: 5. The self-learning promise
options: Bounded standing approval envelope in v2
open_decisions.recommendation: Envelope in v2: 'improves itself within limits you set, and proves what it changes'.

open_decisions.question: 6. Preference memory tier
open_decisions.recommendation: Base, late v1, behind MEM-SIM and the latency A/B.

open_decisions.question: 7. The Operator's name
open_decisions.recommendation: 'VP' for v0.5; test 'Saarthi' after a brand check.

open_decisions.question: 8. Production failover
options: Declared alternate stack on a different provider (section 7.3)
open_decisions.recommendation: Declared alternate, cross-provider before production; tests never fall back.

open_decisions.question: 9. Runtime split
options: Python voice-rt plus TypeScript control plane
open_decisions.recommendation: Python plus TypeScript; reverse if a TypeScript port matches battery latency with less operations work.

open_decisions.question: 10. Regional languages
options: Five betas in v1 on the Indic stack
open_decisions.recommendation: Five betas in v1, each behind its own safety gate.

open_decisions.question: 11. Benchmark voices
options: Add ElevenLabs and Cartesia to the round-2 ear test
open_decisions.recommendation: Add them so 'by ear' means against the best.

open_decisions.question: 12. Fixed-cost recovery
options: INR 500 lifetime trial, credited INR 1,000 first top-up, Operator fair use
open_decisions.recommendation: Trial plus credited top-up and fair use; no seat or platform fee.

open_decisions.question: 13. Spend now
options: Plivo recharge, VP's DLT registration, VP-owned Google organisation, counsel

open_decisions.question: 14. Who builds v0.5
options: Name owners for voice-rt, control plane and design (6-8 week target)
open_decisions.recommendation: Name three owners now; no staffing plan exists yet.

open_decisions.question: 15. Assisted onboarding
options: VP Success included for first 10-20 tenants
open_decisions.recommendation: Include it, through the same tools.

open_decisions.question: 16. The opening spec
options: One spec: name check, then one breath with name, brand, 'AI assistant' in passing and the useful fact
AI clause in the first words
open_decisions.recommendation: Approve the spec and test 2-3 placements on the listener panel; wording may change, presence never; no undisclosed arm.
